title: Role-play lab: six comparison conversations
objectives: Answer six MF/PMS/AIF conversations in plain words in under two minutes.
Use the module's scenario answers (Q21–Q25) as trainer-marked practice.
body_md:
In pairs. One person plays the client, the other explains — in plain words, with a rupee example.

| # | Scenario | What a good response includes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | A client asks, "What's the difference between MF, PMS and AIF, in simple words?" | Minimum ticket, ownership, liquidity, cost and tax, in under two minutes; no jargon. |
| 2 | A ₹60 lakh investor with no MF core wants a PMS "because it's better". | Eligible vs suitable; builds the MF core first; PMS only as a slice later. |
| 3 | A ₹5 crore client wants to put ₹2 crore into a private equity AIF and may need ₹50 lakh in two years for a house. | Explains the lock-in and drawdowns; sizes the AIF so the house money stays liquid. |
| 4 | A client's VC AIF shows a negative return after 18 months; they want out. | Explains the J-curve and closed-ended structure; reviews against the fund's plan; no promises. |
| 5 | A client saw an "AIF with 18% fixed returns" advertised on social media. | Flags that AIFs can't be publicly advertised or promise returns; advises caution; verifies registration. |
| 6 | A client asks why they should keep mutual funds now that they're "wealthy enough" for PMS and AIFs. | Liquidity, cost, diversification and tax efficiency of the MF core; ladder, not replacement. |

> **Investor takeaway:** Quiz scenarios Q21–Q25 (trainer-marked): a scenario answer earns its mark if it covers at least three model points and makes no promise of returns.
example: Role-play the two-minute difference: ticket, ownership, liquidity, cost, tax — ₹100s vs ₹50 lakh vs ₹1 crore, units vs own demat vs units.
say: Minimum ticket, ownership, liquidity, cost and tax, in under two minutes.
never: Move clients up the ladder for commission.

check.q: A client asks, “What's the difference between MF, PMS and AIF?” Explain in under two minutes.
o: Minimum ticket (₹100s / ₹50 lakh / ₹1 crore), ownership (units vs own demat vs units), liquidity, costs and tax, in plain words
They are identical except for the name
check.why: Covers minimum ticket (₹100s / ₹50 L / ₹1 Cr), ownership (units vs own demat vs units), liquidity, costs and tax, in plain words.

check.q: A ₹60 lakh investor with no mutual fund core wants a PMS “because it's better”. How do you respond?
o: Eligible is not suitable; build the MF core and emergency fund first; PMS only later as a slice
Invest everything in the PMS now
check.why: Eligible is not suitable; build the MF core and emergency fund first; PMS only later as a slice.

check.q: A ₹5 crore client wants ₹2 crore in a private equity AIF but may need ₹50 lakh in two years for a house. What do you do?
o: Invest the full ₹2 crore including house money
Explain the lock-in and drawdowns; keep the house money liquid; size the AIF only from money not needed for years
Promise an exit in two years
Use the house money for the AIF
check.why: Explains lock-in and capital calls; keeps the house money liquid; sizes the AIF only from money not needed for years.
